e.etymology: From Arabic muna, wishes or desires, the plural of munya. In Egypt and the Levant it is usually written Mona.
A surname used as a first name in honor of astronomer Carl Sagan, host of the TV series Cosmos and author of Contact.

assoc.t: Carl Sagan, astronomer and host of Cosmos

e.etymology: An elaboration of ocean, from Greek Okeanos, the great river the Greeks believed circled the world.
From the Arabic verb saja, to be calm and still, used in the Quran of the night when it grows quiet.

assoc.t: Saja Boys, demon boy band in KPop Demon Hunters

e.etymology: The Greek and French form of Zipporah, the wife of Moses, from Hebrew tzippor, bird.

assoc.t: Sephora, beauty and cosmetics retail chain

e.note: Most Americans will think first of the Sephora cosmetics stores.

e.etymology: A respelling of Landry, a French surname from the Germanic name Landric: land, land, and ric, ruler.
A Spanish phonetic spelling of the English name Jamie, a pet form of James, used in Latin American families.
A spelling of Alina, a name used across Germany and Eastern Europe that began as a short form of Adelina, from the Germanic element adal, noble.
A modern name that draws on Greek xylon, wood, as Xyla does. Xylia is also a genus of tropical trees.

e.meaning: from Najera, a town in La Rioja, Spain
e.etymology: The Basque name of Najera, a town in La Rioja, Spain, used as a girl's name in honor of the Virgin of Najera. It is popular in Spain and Brazil.
A recent American coinage in the pattern of Jayvion, Davion and Kavion.
A minor biblical name, Hebrew Atsalyahu, usually read as Yahweh has set apart; Azaliah was the father of the scribe Shaphan. For girls today it doubles as a spelling of the flower name Azalea.
From Greek Kalypso, from kalyptein, to cover or hide. In the Odyssey she is the sea nymph who keeps Odysseus on her island for seven years. Calypso is also the carnival music of Trinidad.

assoc.t: calypso, Caribbean music style from Trinidad
sea nymph who detains Odysseus in the Odyssey

e.etymology: The Arabic form of Job, the prophet famed for patience in suffering, who is honored in the Quran. The name also recalls the Ayyubid dynasty of Saladin, son of Najm al-Din Ayyub.
A modern Indian name ending in ansh, Sanskrit for part or portion, the same ending as Reyansh and Shivansh.
A modern American coinage that joins Ty- to the -aire sound of Zaire and Kyaire.
A Japanese girls' name ending in ko, child. Nami is often written with the character for wave, though other kanji with other meanings are also used.
The French form of Michael, from Hebrew Mikhael, who is like God? It is a man's name in French, Dutch and German.
e.note: Michel is the masculine form in French, but Americans often read it as Michelle.

e.meaning: little drop, from an Irish surname
e.etymology: A spelling of Brennan, the English form of the Irish surname O Braonain, descendant of Braonan, a byname from braon, a drop of water.
A Spanish name, most common in Mexico, from the Latinized Germanic name Leobardus, borne by a 6th-century hermit saint near Tours.
The Spanish, Italian and Portuguese form of Augustus, Latin for venerable, the title taken by Octavian, the first Roman emperor.

e.meaning: son, a pet name for a boy
e.etymology: A spelling of Sonny, an affectionate English word for a boy, from son. The -ie spelling was common around 1900 and is also used for girls, sometimes as a form of Sunny.
A short name with several sources: Vietnamese Chi, from Chinese characters for branch; Igbo chi, God or personal spirit, the start of names such as Chidi and Chioma; and Chinese names romanized Chi.

assoc.t: chi (qi), life energy in Chinese philosophy
CHI, flat iron and hair care brand

e.etymology: From Arabic mahir, skilled or expert. The identical-looking Irish surname Maher, as in comedian Bill Maher, is unrelated and comes from O Meachair.
A spelling of Brentley, a modern American blend of Brent and the -ley ending, which took off alongside Bentley around 2010.
The feminine of Farid, from Arabic farid, unique or without equal; farida is also a word for a precious pearl.
From Arabic munir, giving light or radiant, from the same root as nur, light.

e.meaning: blend of Maria and bella, beautiful
e.etymology: A blend of Maria and Bella, or a lengthening of Maribel, the Spanish contraction of Maria Isabel, with the Italian-style -bella, beautiful.
A modern feminine name that reads as Evan or Eva with a -ny ending, close to Evanie and Evanna.

e.meaning: desired, longed for (via Desiree and Desiderio)
e.etymology: A z spelling of Desi, short for Desiree and Desiderio, both from Latin desiderium, longing, and also for Desmond. Bandleader Desi Arnaz was born Desiderio.
An Italian pet form of Gianna, itself short for Giovanna, the feminine of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
A modern American name that blends Lamar with Amir, or adds the La- prefix to the -mir of Jamir and Samir.
